title: Knight After Knight
author: SingingFish
rules:
Hi, this is one of the more conceptual ideas for a sudoku ruleset I have had. I had lots of joy teasing out logic and thinking about the implications of these specific rules. As with some of these more geometric constructions I think there is some deeper underlying pattern/logic going on here than might be necessary to solve the thing. In addition, I am really not sure as to how difficult people may find this so I have just provisionally gone with 3 stars. In any case hopefully you find it interesting and fun to solve. Enjoy :)

==============================================

Rules:

Normal 6×6 Sudoku rules apply.

Kropki dots:

Digits in cells joined by a white dot are consecutive.

Digits in cells joined by a black dot are in a 1:2 ratio.

Cyclically Consecutive Knights:

Every cell must have at least two cells a chess knight's move away containing digits consecutive to its own.

For this rule, consecutiveness is cyclic (1-2-3-4-5-6-1), meaning 1 and 6 are also considered consecutive.

This cyclic rule does not apply to Kropki dots.

Left is valid (no issue with the consecutive digits being the same)

Middle is valid (shows cyclic nature in the rule and that 2 consecutive digits is a minimum and 3,4,5 etc is fine)

Right is invalid (cell has only 1 consecutive digit a knight's move away)
